turns.assistant_text:
Here are some recent news articles about AI from this week:

1. **[Voters deliver "AI earthquake," rebuking tech and billionaires](https://www.axios.com/2026/11/04/ai-data-center-election-slowdown)** - AI has emerged as a significant issue in American politics, with voters showing distrust towards the AI race. Many approved data center moratoriums and elected candidates favoring a slowdown in AI development, viewing it as a threat to their communities and wallets. (Source: Axios)

2. **[Google to end search access for schools that block its AI tools, sparking backlash](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/google-search-access-schools-ai-tools)** - Google is facing criticism for its decision to restrict search access for schools that do not utilize its AI tools. This move has raised concerns about the implications of AI in educational settings. (Source: CBS News)

3. **[A single AI model simulates the behavior of many substances, from sliding sand to folding proteins](https://news.mit.edu/2026/single-ai-model-simulates-many-substances-behavior-1109)** - Researchers have developed a unified AI architecture capable of simulating various physical phenomena, learning the underlying dynamics rather than relying on pre-programmed equations. This advancement could enhance the understanding of material behaviors. (Source: MIT News)

4. **[IBM and Microsoft announce a new AI agent platform designed for industry-specific transformation](https://news.microsoft.com/source/2026/11/10/ibm-and-microsoft-announce-a-new-ai-agent-platform-designed-for-industry-specific-transformation)** - IBM and Microsoft have introduced a new AI platform aimed at transforming industries by integrating human expertise with digital labor, focusing on creating competitive advantages through AI. (Source: Microsoft News)

If you need more information or further articles, feel free to ask!

items.title: Voters deliver "AI earthquake," rebuking tech and billionaires
items.summary:
AI had its "official debut" as the biggest issue in American politics, former New York Assemblymember and RAISE Act author Alex Bores told Axios. "AI is reaching into every part of our society and economy and it's now crystal clear it's impacting every part of our politics, too." [...] Voters showed deep distrust of the AI race Tuesday, approving dozens of data center moratoriums and electing a raft of candidates who favor slowing a $10 trillion buildout, including in Texas — the epicenter of the boom.

Why it matters: In an election that hinged on an affordability crisis for many Americans, voters made it clear they view Silicon Valley's AI ambitions not as a technological miracle, but as a resource-draining threat to their wallets and communities. [...] Democratic challengers successfully weaponized AI policy, ousting Republicans in Ohio, Wisconsin, Arizona and Pennsylvania.
   Democratic groups had poured ads into these districts attacking GOP incumbents for a 2025 vote that would've neutered state AI legislation.
   AI safety advocates won or were poised to win races on Tuesday that will expand their coalition in the new Congress, including Colorado's Manny Rutinel and Minnesota's Matt Little.

items.title: A single AI model simulates the behavior of many substances, from sliding sand to folding proteins | MIT News | Massachusetts Institute of Technology
items.summary:
Unified simulation

For this work, the researchers drew inspiration from world models. These powerful AI systems learn the rules that govern the physical world so they can predict how objects or environments will change over time in response to certain actions or conditions.

The researchers applied these concepts to develop a unified AI architecture that can simulate multiple types of physical phenomena. [...] ## More MIT News

Robot serving a cup of coffee while being instructed not to spill on the laptop

### AI-assisted learning platform helps robots reason beyond literal commands

The new approach, known as FLEX, could lead to more intuitive, interactive household and assistive robots.

Read full story →

Man wearing a T-shirt and safety goggles standing above a concrete beam in the lab, operating a bench-mounted laser tool scanning the concrete. [...] The system represents every material it simulates, from a dune of sand to a protein molecule, as tiny particles and predicts where those particles will move one step at a time. Because it learns the underlying dynamics rather than being programmed with an equation, the model can adapt to materials, forces, and environments it never encountered during training.

items.title: IBM and Microsoft announce a new AI agent platform designed for industry-specific transformation - Source
items.summary: “Clients are no longer looking for AI that simply helps people do the same work a little faster. They want to build an agentic business,” said Mohamad Ali, Senior Vice President and Head of IBM Consulting. “Microsoft and IBM are helping organizations bring human expertise and digital labor together in a way that can scale across the enterprise, to turn AI from a productivity aid into a real competitive advantage.” [...] “AI is evolving quickly, and our focus at SEI is on applying it with intention in ways that strengthen trust, enhance human decision-making and create meaningful value across our business,” said Sneha Shah, Chief AI Strategist and Head of SEI Next. “Our work with IBM Consulting and Microsoft is helping us explore how emerging capabilities could support critical processes and be responsibly scaled over time, with the goal to create better experiences for our employees and clients. By combining [...] “Enterprise AI will be won by organizations that can turn their data, industry expertise and AI into action,” said Rodrigo Kede Lima, President, Microsoft Frontier Company. “Together, Microsoft and IBM Consulting are bringing the best of our technology and expertise, to help customers move from AI ambition to business impact faster and with confidence.”
